history.text: The Kingdom of Dahomey rose at Abomey and became a major regional power.
Ouidah served as one of the busiest slave-trading ports on the Bight of Benin.
France completed its conquest and made Dahomey a colony.
The country was governed as a Marxist-Leninist state and renamed Benin.
A national conference led to multi-party elections and a peaceful transfer of power.

worthSeeing.title: Royal Palaces of Abomey:
worthSeeing.text: The earthen palaces of the Dahomey kings, a UNESCO World Heritage site.

worthSeeing.title: Ganvie:
worthSeeing.text: A lake village on Lake Nokoue built on stilts and reached by pirogue.

worthSeeing.title: Ouidah:
worthSeeing.text: The Door of No Return and the slave route running from town to the beach.
